basics.description: Access Review portal in your existing virtual network. The web app, PostgreSQL and Key Vault get private endpoints and have no public access. The template creates no virtual network and no subnets. Choose the region of your virtual network.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: The region of your virtual network. All resources and private endpoints are created in this region.

options.text: Before you start: the app registration (client ID and secret), a subnet for App Service and a subnet for private endpoints in your virtual network, and the DNS plan for the private endpoints. Select this box to open the guide.
Choose your virtual network and its subnets. The template creates no virtual network and no subnets. The list shows the virtual networks in the region above, in all subscriptions that you can read.

elements.name: vnet
elements.label: Virtual network
elements.toolTip: The virtual network with the subnets. It must be in the region above.

elements.name: appSubnet
elements.label: App Service subnet
elements.toolTip: VNet integration of the web app: all its outbound traffic goes through this subnet. The list shows the subnets that are delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. /28 or larger, /26 recommended.

options.text: This virtual network has no subnet delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. Ask your network team to delegate an empty subnet (/27 or /26): Subnets > the subnet > Subnet delegation > Microsoft.Web/serverFarms. The subnet is then only for App Service.

elements.name: endpointMode
elements.label: Private endpoint subnets
elements.defaultValue: One subnet for all private endpoints
elements.toolTip: One subnet: the private endpoints of the web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and the registry are in one subnet. A subnet for each service: you choose the subnet of each private endpoint, for example when your network has separate subnets for application and data endpoints.

allowedValues.label: One subnet for all private endpoints

elements.name: endpointSubnet
elements.label: Private endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: The private endpoints of the web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and, for a container, the registry: one IP address each. The list shows the subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

elements.name: siteEndpointSubnet
elements.label: Web app endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: Subnet of the private endpoint pe-<App name>. Users and the deployment workflow reach the portal through it. The list shows the subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

elements.name: postgresEndpointSubnet
elements.label: PostgreSQL endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: Subnet of the private endpoint pe-<server name> of the PostgreSQL server. The list shows the subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

elements.name: vaultEndpointSubnet
elements.label: Key Vault endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: Subnet of the private endpoint of the Key Vault: a new vault, or your existing vault when the template creates a private endpoint for it (section Key Vault). The list shows the subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

elements.name: registryEndpointSubnet
elements.label: Registry endpoint subnet
elements.toolTip: Container image only: subnet of the private endpoint of the registry, a new registry or your existing registry when the template creates a private endpoint for it (section Container registry). The list shows the subnets without delegation.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.subnets, parse('[]')), (s) => and(not(contains(parse('["GatewaySubnet","AzureFirewallSubnet","AzureFirewallManagementSubnet","AzureBastionSubnet","RouteServerSubnet"]'), s.name)), empty(s.properties.delegations))), (s) => parse(concat('{"label":"', s.name, ' (', coalesce(s.properties.addressPrefix, ''), ')","value":"', s.id, '"}')))]

options.text: [if(equals(basics('network').endpointMode, 'each'), 'The template creates the private endpoint of each service in the subnet that you choose for it. None of the services has public access. The subnet of a private endpoint cannot be changed later: to move it, delete the private endpoint and deploy again.', 'The template creates its private endpoints in this subnet: web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and, for a container, the registry. None of them has public access.')]
Choose two different subnets. The App Service subnet is only for App Service.

elements.name: appName
elements.label: App name
elements.toolTip: Name of the web app. The portal address is https://<App name>.azurewebsites.net. Must be unique in Azure.

validations.message: 2-58 characters: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. No hyphen at the start or the end.

options.text: [concat('This name is already in use: ', basics('app').nameApi.message, ' If it is your own web app from an earlier attempt of this deployment, continue: the deployment updates it. Otherwise choose another name.')]

elements.name: appServicePlanSku
elements.label: App Service plan size
elements.toolTip: P0v3 is enough for most tenants. See docs/SIZING.md.

elements.name: zoneRedundant
elements.label: Zone redundancy
elements.toolTip: Azure spreads the instances over the availability zones of the region and chooses the zones. App Service has no setting to choose a zone. Needs a Premium plan and a region with availability zones. Decide before the first deployment: an existing plan cannot always be changed later.

allowedValues.label: On: 3 instances, one in each zone

options.text: Zone redundancy needs a Premium plan (P0v3 or larger). Choose a P plan size.
This region has no availability zones. Choose Off, or another region.
This region has only two availability zones. Azure puts two of the three instances in the same zone.

elements.name: deploymentType
elements.label: Deployment
elements.toolTip: Code package: the workflow deploy-appservice.yml uploads the built app. Container image: the web app runs the image from Azure Container Registry, where Microsoft Defender for Cloud scans it; the workflow deploy-appservice-container.yml builds and pushes it.

allowedValues.label: Container image from Azure Container Registry

options.text: The web app pulls the image through your network with its managed identity id-<App name>. Choose the registry in the section Container registry. Until the first run of the workflow deploy-appservice-container.yml, the web app has no image and answers 503.

elements.name: clientId
elements.label: Client ID
elements.toolTip: Application (client) ID of the app registration of the portal.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter the GUID of the application (client) ID.

elements.name: clientSecret
elements.toolTip: Value of a client secret of the app registration. The template stores it in Key Vault.

elements.name: databaseServer
elements.label: Database server
elements.toolTip: Azure Database for PostgreSQL: the template creates the server with a private endpoint. Your own server: for example PostgreSQL on a VM; the template creates no server.

options.text: The server has no public access. The template creates its private endpoint pe-<server name> in the private endpoint subnet (Network section) and the DNS record in the zone privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com (Private DNS zones section).

elements.name: databaseAuthentication
elements.label: Sign-in to PostgreSQL
elements.toolTip: Managed identity: the identity id-<App name> of the web app is the Microsoft Entra administrator of the server. The server accepts no passwords.

elements.name: postgresAdminPassword
elements.toolTip: Password of the administrator login accessreviewadmin. The template stores the connection string in Key Vault.

elements.name: postgresServerName
elements.label: Server name
elements.toolTip: Name of the PostgreSQL server in Azure, unique in Azure, lower case. Empty: psql-<App name>. The deployment step that creates it is named postgres-<server name>.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-63 characters: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

elements.name: postgresSize
elements.label: Compute size
elements.toolTip: General Purpose D2ds_v5 is enough for most tenants and is available in all regions. Burstable is cheaper but not available for every subscription in every region. See docs/SIZING.md.

elements.name: highAvailability
elements.label: High availability
elements.toolTip: Zone redundant: a standby server in another availability zone takes over automatically. Same zone: standby in the same zone. The standby doubles the compute cost. Not with Burstable sizes.

elements.name: availabilityZone
elements.label: Availability zone
elements.toolTip: Zone of the PostgreSQL server. No preference: Azure chooses. Azure uses the zone only when it creates the server. A later deployment with another zone does not move the server.

elements.name: standbyZone
elements.label: Standby availability zone
elements.toolTip: Zone of the standby server, another zone than the server. No preference: Azure chooses.

options.text: The standby server must be in another zone than the server. Choose another standby zone, or No preference.
This region has no availability zones. Choose No preference for the zones.

[concat('vCore quota of your subscription in this region: ', string(first(map(filter(coalesce(basics('database').usagesApi.value, parse('[]')), (u) => equals(u.name.value, if(contains(basics('database').postgresSize, 'Standard_B'), 'standardBSFamily', if(contains(basics('database').postgresSize, 'ads_v5'), 'standardDADSv5Family', if(contains(basics('database').postgresSize, 'Standard_E'), 'standardEDSv5Family', 'standardDDSv5Family'))))), (u) => sub(u.limit, u.currentValue)))), ' free for this size family, ', string(first(map(filter(coalesce(basics('database').usagesApi.value, parse('[]')), (u) => equals(u.name.value, 'cores')), (u) => sub(u.limit, u.currentValue)))), ' free in total. This server needs ', string(mul(if(contains(basics('database').postgresSize, 'D4'), 4, 2), if(equals(basics('database').highAvailability, 'Disabled'), 1, 2))), ' (a standby with high availability counts double).')]
PostgreSQL Flexible Server is restricted in this region for your subscription. Choose another region, or ask Azure support to enable the region.
This size is not offered in this region. Choose another size.
High availability is not possible with Burstable sizes. Choose a General Purpose size, or turn high availability off.
Zone-redundant high availability is not supported in this region. Choose Same zone or Disabled.
Not enough vCore quota for this size family in this region (see the quota line above). Choose another size family, or ask for more quota (Help + support > Service and subscription limits).
Not enough total PostgreSQL vCore quota in this region (see the quota line above). Ask for more quota, or choose a smaller size.

The red messages above come from the PostgreSQL offer and the vCore quota of your subscription in this region. Some limits are visible only when Azure creates the server (error SkuNotAvailable). The template creates PostgreSQL first: then the deployment stops after about two minutes, before it creates anything else. Choose another size and deploy again with the same values.

elements.name: postgresStorageSizeGB
elements.label: Storage
elements.toolTip: Storage auto-grow is on.

options.text: Prepare your server first: a login that owns the database accessreview, TLS, a pg_hba.conf line for the address range of the App Service subnet, and port 5432 open from this subnet.

elements.name: existingServerConnectionString
elements.toolTip: Example: Host=pg01.contoso.com;Port=5432;Database=accessreview;Username=accessreview;Password=<password>;Ssl Mode=VerifyFull. The template stores it in Key Vault.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an Npgsql connection string, for example Host=pg01.contoso.com;Port=5432;Database=accessreview;Username=accessreview;Password=<password>;Ssl Mode=VerifyFull

elements.name: existingServerCaCertificate
elements.label: CA certificate (optional)
elements.toolTip: Only when the server certificate comes from your own CA: the CA certificate as base64 of the .cer file, or PEM. Needed for Ssl Mode=VerifyFull.

options.text: The web app reads the client secret and the database connection string from Key Vault with its managed identity id-<App name>, which gets the role Key Vault Secrets User.

elements.name: vaultMode
elements.label: Key Vault
elements.toolTip: A new vault only for the portal, or your existing vault that uses Azure RBAC.

elements.name: networkAccess
elements.label: Network access
elements.defaultValue: Private endpoint only (public network access disabled)
elements.toolTip: The Key Vault gets a private endpoint in the private endpoint subnet (Network section) and its DNS record in the zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net (Private DNS zones section). Public network access is disabled, with no exceptions.

allowedValues.label: Private endpoint only (public network access disabled)

elements.name: resourceGroupMode
elements.label: Resource group
elements.defaultValue: Same resource group as the portal
elements.toolTip: The Key Vault, its private endpoint and the role assignment go to this resource group.

allowedValues.label: Same resource group as the portal

elements.name: resourceGroup
elements.label: Key Vault resource group
elements.toolTip: An existing resource group in the subscription chosen above.

options.text: You need Contributor and Role Based Access Control Administrator on this resource group too.

elements.name: keyVaultName
elements.label: Key Vault name
elements.placeholder: Empty: a name derived from the resource group and the app name
elements.toolTip: 3-24 characters, unique in Azure. Empty: kv-<unique string>.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-24 characters: letters, digits and hyphens. Starts with a letter.

elements.name: enablePurgeProtection
elements.label: Purge protection
elements.toolTip: With purge protection, a deleted vault and its name stay reserved for 90 days. Recommended for production.

body.query: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.keyvault/vaults' | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | project subscriptionId, subscriptionName = name) on subscriptionId | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups' | project subscriptionId, resourceGroup = tolower(name), groupName = name) on subscriptionId, resourceGroup | project id, name, resourceGroup = coalesce(groupName, resourceGroup), subscription = coalesce(subscriptionName, subscriptionId), location, rbac = tostring(properties.enableRbacAuthorization), publicAccess = iff(isempty(tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess)), 'Enabled', tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess)), endpoints = coalesce(array_length(properties.privateEndpointConnections), 0) | order by name asc

elements.name: existingVault
elements.label: Existing Key Vault
elements.toolTip: The vaults in the subscriptions that you can read: name (resource group, subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(coalesce(basics('keyVault').vaultsApi.data, parse('[]')), (v) => parse(concat('{"label":"', v.name, ' (', v.resourceGroup, ', ', v.subscription, ')","value":"', v.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No Key Vault found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create a new Key Vault, or ask for Reader on the vault.

This vault uses access policies. The template gives access with Azure RBAC only. Switch the vault to Azure role-based access control (Settings > Access configuration), or choose another vault. The switch changes the access of all apps that use the vault.

[first(map(filter(coalesce(basics('keyVault').vaultsApi.data, parse('[]')), (v) => equals(v.id, basics('keyVault').existingVault)), (v) => concat('Region of the vault: ', v.location, '. Public network access: ', v.publicAccess, '. Private endpoints: ', string(v.endpoints), '.')))]

elements.name: existingVaultAccess
elements.label: Access of the web app
elements.defaultValue: Only the two secrets of the portal
elements.toolTip: Scope of the role Key Vault Secrets User for id-<App name>. Only the two secrets: recommended when other apps use the vault.

allowedValues.label: Only the two secrets of the portal

elements.name: existingVaultEndpoint
elements.label: Private endpoint
elements.defaultValue: Not needed: the vault has one that the App Service subnet reaches
elements.toolTip: The web app reads the secrets through your network. Create one only when no private endpoint of the vault is reachable from the App Service subnet.

allowedValues.label: Not needed: the vault has one that the App Service subnet reaches
Create one in the private endpoint subnet

options.text: The vault already has a private endpoint. A new one writes the address of the vault into the zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net (section Private DNS zones). With a central zone, this changes the address for all networks that use the zone.

The template adds the secrets <App name>-client-secret and <App name>-db-connection to this vault and changes nothing else. You need Key Vault Contributor (or Contributor) and Role Based Access Control Administrator on the vault.
The web app runs the image <registry>/access-review-portal. Microsoft Defender for Containers or Defender CSPM scans the images in the registry.

elements.name: registryMode
elements.label: Registry
elements.toolTip: A new registry only for the portal, or your existing registry.

options.text: Premium tier (needed for private endpoints): private endpoint in the private endpoint subnet, no public access, no admin user. Trusted Microsoft services keep access, so Defender for Cloud can scan the images. The managed identity id-<App name> gets AcrPull.

elements.name: registryName
elements.label: Registry name
elements.toolTip: 5-50 letters and digits, unique in Azure. Empty: cr<unique string>.

body.query: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.containerregistry/registries' | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | project subscriptionId, subscriptionName = name) on subscriptionId | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups' | project subscriptionId, resourceGroup = tolower(name), groupName = name) on subscriptionId, resourceGroup | project id, name, resourceGroup = coalesce(groupName, resourceGroup), subscription = coalesce(subscriptionName, subscriptionId), location, sku = tostring(sku.name), mode = tostring(properties.roleAssignmentMode), bypass = tostring(properties.networkRuleBypassOptions), publicAccess = tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess), endpoints = coalesce(array_length(properties.privateEndpointConnections), 0) | order by name asc

elements.name: existingRegistry
elements.label: Existing registry
elements.toolTip: The registries in the subscriptions that you can read: name (resource group, subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(coalesce(basics('registry').registriesApi.data, parse('[]')), (r) => parse(concat('{"label":"', r.name, ' (', r.resourceGroup, ', ', r.subscription, ')","value":"', r.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No container registry found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create a new registry, or ask for Reader on the registry.

[first(map(filter(coalesce(basics('registry').registriesApi.data, parse('[]')), (r) => equals(r.id, basics('registry').existingRegistry)), (r) => concat('Region of the registry: ', r.location, '. Tier: ', r.sku, '. Public network access: ', r.publicAccess, '. Private endpoints: ', string(r.endpoints), '.')))]

This registry uses ABAC repository permissions. id-<App name> gets Container Registry Repository Reader instead of AcrPull. The GitHub identity of the workflow needs Container Registry Repository Writer instead of AcrPush.
Trusted Microsoft services have no access to this registry. Defender for Cloud scans the images of a registry without public access only when trusted services may access it (Networking > Exceptions).

elements.name: existingRegistryEndpoint
elements.label: Private endpoint
elements.defaultValue: Not needed: the registry has one that the App Service subnet reaches
elements.toolTip: The web app pulls the image through your network. Create one only when no private endpoint of the registry is reachable from the App Service subnet.

allowedValues.label: Not needed: the registry has one that the App Service subnet reaches
Create one in the private endpoint subnet

options.text: Private endpoints need the Premium tier. Choose Not needed, or another registry.

The registry already has a private endpoint. A new one writes the addresses of the registry into the zone privatelink.azurecr.io (section Private DNS zones). With a central zone, this changes the addresses for all networks that use the zone.
The template gives id-<App name> the pull role on this registry and changes nothing else. You need Role Based Access Control Administrator on the registry, and Contributor for a new private endpoint.

After the deployment, give the GitHub identity of the workflow the role AcrPush on the registry (Container Registry Repository Writer with ABAC repository permissions), and set the workflow variable ACR_LOGIN_SERVER (template output containerRegistryLoginServer).

elements.name: dnsMode
elements.label: Zones
elements.toolTip: New zones: the template creates the zones that its private endpoints need (privatelink.azurewebsites.net, privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com, privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net, privatelink.azurecr.io) in the resource group and links them to the virtual network. Existing zones: your central zones, for example in a hub subscription.

options.text: [concat('This virtual network uses custom DNS servers (', string(basics('network').vnetApi.properties.dhcpOptions.dnsServers), '). New zones in this resource group are linked only to this virtual network, so these DNS servers do not see them. Use the existing zones that your DNS servers resolve.')]

Users open the portal from your network. Your DNS must resolve <App name>.azurewebsites.net to the private endpoint, for example with a conditional forwarder for privatelink.azurewebsites.net to an Azure DNS resolver.

body.query: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/privatednszones' and name in~ ('privatelink.azurewebsites.net', 'privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com', 'privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net', 'privatelink.azurecr.io') | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | project subscriptionId, subscriptionName = name) on subscriptionId | join kind=leftouter (resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups' | project subscriptionId, resourceGroup = tolower(name), groupName = name) on subscriptionId, resourceGroup | project id, name, resourceGroup = coalesce(groupName, resourceGroup), subscription = coalesce(subscriptionName, subscriptionId) | order by subscription asc, resourceGroup asc

elements.name: siteZone
elements.label: Zone privatelink.azurewebsites.net
elements.toolTip: The zones with this name in the subscriptions that you can read: resource group (subscription).

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(basics('dns').zonesApi.data, parse('[]')), (z) => equals(toLower(z.name), 'privatelink.azurewebsites.net')), (z) => parse(concat('{"label":"', z.resourceGroup, ' (', z.subscription, ')","value":"', z.id, '"}')))]

options.text: No zone privatelink.azurewebsites.net found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create new zones, or ask for Reader on the zone.

options.text: No zone privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com found in the subscriptions that you can read. Choose Create new zones, or ask for Reader on the zone.
